verdicts.matching_evidence: In Section I.C, the running reduced $\chi^2$ statistic is defined as $\chi^2_n(\theta) = \frac{1}{n} \sum_{i=1}^{n} \frac{(x_i - \hat{x}(\theta))^2}{2\hat{\sigma}^2(\theta)}$. The factor of $2$ in the denominator is mathematically incorrect for a standard $\chi^2$ definition. While a $2\sigma^2$ denominator correctly appears inside the exponent of a Gaussian likelihood function, the statistical $\chi^2$ sum itself evaluates variance solely as $\sigma^2$.
